qs.q: Analysis of the tumour microenvironment (TME) in a patient with advanced breast cancer reveals a population of M2-polarised tumour-associated macrophages. What is the primary role of these cells within the TME?
o: Promoting tumour growth, suppressing immunity, and driving angiogenesis
Secreting thrombospondin-1 to inhibit local blood vessel growth
Directly functioning as cancer stem cells with CD44+/CD24- markers
Reversing epigenetic DNA methylation by acting as methyltransferases
qs.e: M2-polarised tumour-associated macrophages promote tumour progression, suppress the host immune response, and facilitate angiogenesis. Thrombospondin-1 is an anti-angiogenic factor, not secreted by these pro-tumourigenic immune cells.
